nodes.natural_language: f(x) = sqrt(a x^2 + b x) with b > 0
nodes.statement: Domain D = {x in R | a x^2 + b x >= 0} and range R = f(D) must satisfy D = R as sets.

nodes.natural_language: D must be a closed interval [0, M] or [0, +inf) for some M
nodes.statement: D is [0, +inf) or [0, M] (M finite) because b > 0 forces 0 in D and D unbounded above or bounded by root -b/a.

nodes.natural_language: f maps D onto [0, sup f) or [0, sup f]
nodes.statement: Range equals [0, lim x->inf f(x)) or [0, f(x_max)] depending on a sign and vertex location.

nodes.natural_language: Case a = 0 forces D = [0, +inf) and range = [0, +inf) only if b arbitrary positive
nodes.statement: a = 0 yields D = [0, +inf) and range = [0, +inf), satisfying equality.

nodes.natural_language: Case a < 0 yields bounded D = [0, -b/a] and quadratic max forces range match only for specific a = -b/4
nodes.statement: a < 0 produces exactly one a = -1/4 satisfying range = D after scaling b = 1.

nodes.natural_language: Case a > 0 yields D unbounded or empty; range never matches D except impossible limits
nodes.statement: a > 0 produces no solutions because range is bounded while D is unbounded or range misses 0 endpoint.

nodes.natural_language: Exactly two real a (namely a = 0 and a = -1/4) admit at least one b > 0 making domain equal range
nodes.statement: Number of valid real a is 2.

nodes.natural_language: The range of f is contained in [0,\infty), so if the domain D equals the range then necessarily D\subseteq[0,\infty).
Consequently D={x:ax^{2}+bx\ge0} and this set must be contained in the non-negative reals.
nodes.statement: D = {x \in ℝ | a x^{2} + b x \ge 0} \subseteq [0,\infty).
